claims: MediaProjection sends captured screen or app-window content to a VirtualDisplay backed by an app-provided Surface.
Android14 requires fresh user consent for each projection session and a token permits one createVirtualDisplay call.
onCapturedContentResize supplies dimensions; both VirtualDisplay and output Surface must be resized to avoid letterboxing.
onStop invalidates the session and requires resource release.
acquireLatestImage drops older queued images and is intended for realtime consumption.
Dropping older images requires maxImages-currentAcquiredImages >=2; unreleased images can exhaust the queue.
ImageReader.close invalidates its images and previously acquired pixel buffers.
The HardwareBuffer returned by Image.getHardwareBuffer must not be used after Image.close.
Image timestamps are in nanoseconds, but sources can use different timebases.
HardwareBuffer.close releases native resources and forbids further use.
A Surface is a producer handle tied to a buffer consumer.
A Surface alone does not retain its SurfaceTexture/consumer; its local reference must be released.
Stream attaches external video frames to a Texture.
ACQUIRED streams accept Android hardware buffers, synchronize with the scene and release through callbacks.
NATIVE streams have no synchronization guarantee.
